A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DEFOM-Stereo. All 17 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including their supplementary material, support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures. Relocated and renumbered content can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original stereo benchmark results, zero-shot evaluations, component ablations, depth-alignment analysis, and qualitative experiments, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds regional error analysis, RVC visual comparisons, and reflective/transparent-surface case studies.

M1.justification: The CNN/DPT feature fusion, monocular depth initialization, scale lookup, multiplicative scale updates, additive delta updates, and training objective remain unchanged in Section 3. Newly specifying the initialization epsilon does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds qualitative evaluation on Booster scenes containing transparent, reflective, and large-mirror surfaces. Booster previously appeared only in the RVC training mixture. The other training datasets and evaluation domains are retained.

E2.justification: The Scene Flow comparison against six methods in v1 Table 2 is removed. Qualitative comparisons on the four standard datasets add Mocha-Stereo and Selective-IGEV, and Flickr1024 comparisons add Selective-IGEV. The main numerical zero-shot, official benchmark, and RVC comparator sets otherwise remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces separate Middlebury-half Bad 2.0 evaluations for non-occluded, occluded, and textureless regions, with SSIM-based textureless masks and region proportions. Existing training budgets, resolutions, iteration counts, and stated evaluation masks remain unchanged; revised Middlebury scores alone do not establish a changed protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendices D–F substantially expand diagnostic evidence: RVC visual comparisons, quantitative occlusion/textureless-region analysis with error maps, and reflective/transparent-surface cases exposing large-mirror failures. The original encoder-design and scale-update-iteration ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or training-seed counts. The depth-alignment ratio standard deviations are unchanged and move from v1 Table 1 to v2 Table 6; they measure spatial scale inconsistency.

E6.justification: Substantial Middlebury revisions affect zero-shot results and component ablations. In v1 Table 3 versus v2 Table 1, ViT-L full/half/quarter Bad 2.0 changes from 8.51/3.26/3.27 to 11.95/5.91/5.65; Mocha-Stereo half-resolution error changes from 9.11 to 11.49. Depth initialization changes from 9.40 to 12.40 against an unchanged 10.67 baseline. V2 also adds regional results and removes the Scene Flow comparison table. Official benchmark and RVC numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The method equations and Appendix A's affine-alignment and ratio definitions are retained. V2 adds no theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive mathematical revision; diagram notation changes are presentational.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its illustrative Middlebury error-reduction claim from 'over a half' to 'about a third.' The principal framework, generalization, and leaderboard claims remain. The abstract drops the explicit Scene Flow comparability statement, although that claim remains in the introduction.

C2.justification: V2 adds a conjecture connecting scale inconsistency to training across different fields of view with affine-invariant loss. Appendix F newly qualifies applicability: less severe reflective/transparent scenes can work, but large mirrors can defeat the model. V1 lacked this explicit failure discussion.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies epsilon = 0.05 for disparity initialization. Appendix E documents SSIM-based textureless-region extraction, and the front-page access link changes from a repository to a project page. Existing hardware, optimizer, learning rate, and training-budget disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Stereo Anywhere, MonSter, and FoundationStereo as contemporary work, contrasting their IGEV-style initialization with direct DEFOM depth initialization and revised recurrent updates. Appendix F also positions Stereo Anywhere as relevant to difficult mirror/transparent scenes. These citations do not constitute new numerical baseline evaluations.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized abstract and introduction rewrites, refocuses Section 4.2 on zero-shot generalization, moves the depth-alignment table and discussion into Appendix A, and adds Appendices D–F. Most methodological exposition and the conclusion remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 substantially rebuilds the qualitative presentation: a main-text comparison is added, benchmark and Flickr1024 panels are reorganized and expanded, and new RVC, regional-error, and Booster figures appear. It also clarifies Figure 3's operator legend and replaces incorrectly displayed Scene Flow input panels in v1 Figure 4 with RGB inputs in v2 Figure 5. The depth-alignment table is relocated and the Scene Flow comparison table removed.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful regional diagnostics, contemporary positioning, and explicit mirror-failure evidence. However, its revised Middlebury results introduce unresolved reporting inconsistencies: Section 4.3 still claims depth initialization improves performance despite 12.40 versus 10.67 error, whereas v1's 9.40 supported that claim. The main full-model error also becomes 6.76 while Appendix B retains 4.287 without explaining different evaluation conditions. These central consistency problems coexist with stronger diagnostic coverage, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
